lead: the estimate goes out on the day you walk the site, and it is believed, and the outfit the client has been picturing while you talked has eleven people in it. you run four.
sun: nothing you say in that first hour sizes the shop correctly, because the sizing finished before you spoke — off the width you take up in a doorway, off the amount of you out at once. so the job lands above your weight every single time, scoped for a firm with a yard and a scheduler in it, and signed by a client who did not think to ask how many vans there are.
moon: getting there first is the reflex under it. you are on the site before the keys, at the meeting before there is an agenda, offering a date while the problem is still being described — and speed reads as competence stacked behind the size. what you have done is arrive. sequencing, lead times, whether the shop can take it that quarter: that gets worked out on the drive back.
pull: you did not win the job. the doorway won it, and the date you gave on the phone won it, and the four people who have to build the thing were not in the room.
tension: overpromising is the charge, and it is close enough to true that arguing looks like arguing. you inflated nothing. you turned up early, gave an honest date for a job you had looked at for forty minutes, and let somebody do arithmetic on a shop they had never visited. the shortfall that opens in week three is real and it gets eaten, and the people eating it are a crew the client has never met.
cost: work walks toward you that a business of four does not get offered — unsolicited, from clients who found you rather than the other way round. nobody checks the size of a thing that reads solid. no one has asked about your capacity in nine years, so the only person awake to whether it can actually be done is you, at eleven at night, with the paper already signed.

lead: your sister's carefulness at the table is the loudest thing in the room, and she has never put a word to it, and both of you know precisely which years the money went where.
sun: the family bet on you early, before you had done anything to be bet on — you were six and visitors looked at you, and a household decided from that where its margin was going. the lessons, the deposit, the second chance at twenty-two nobody else was offered. it still runs that way at every gathering: relatives ask you how everyone is doing, on the grounds that you look like the one who would know.
moon: and you do know, because it gets brought to you. a person who reads that large gets handed the diagnosis and the arrears and the thing about the marriage on the assumption that it will fit inside, and it does fit. it goes in, and the day it comes back out is yours to name, and mostly you do not. nobody outside four people knows the house is being sold.
pull: the family handed you the largest share and then handed you everything it could not say aloud, and it has never occurred to a single one of them that those were two separate transfers.
tension: at the wedding an uncle called you spoiled, affectionately, into a microphone, and the room laughed because the room agreed. no one can produce the moment you asked for more — it was decided over you before you could speak. and the ones who got less have been gentle with you for thirty years, and the gentleness is worse than an accusation, because an accusation is answerable and gentleness is not.
cost: a thing gets given to you late on a sunday and by morning nothing shows, which is exactly why it comes to you rather than to each other. the register never drops, though. asking would require a smaller voice than you were issued, and the one evening you went near it, at a cousin's kitchen, three people told you that you were the strong one and topped up your glass.

lead: there is no single number to give. there are six, no salary among them, two arriving from people who would be insulted to be called a source — and from any distance the six resolve into one solid figure.
sun: the figure gets set before you have opened your mouth about money, and it gets set high. you are quoted the upper price, seated where the bill lands, brought into things at a level nobody cleared with you. none of that is anyone behaving badly. it is a sum done off the size that is showing, and nothing about the size is adjustable.
moon: inside, it is six small things standing in a line, and the smallness does not transmit at any distance. one of the six ends in spring and you have known since last autumn. the whole arrangement could be counted in an afternoon by anyone who bothered, and the reason nobody bothers is that a thing reading as one large amount does not look like it has parts that fail separately.
pull: the room prices you at the total, and the total is accurate. it is also six things that can each end on a phone call, and not a person alive has asked you which.
tension: you decline a weekend away and it plays as meanness, because from where they sit there is no other explanation on offer. the true sentence — that the number is plural, that two parts of it are somebody's kindness — comes out of somebody built like you as a bid for sympathy. so you would rather be thought tight, and you pay, and you go home and move the sum from the stream that could not spare it.
cost: one of the six collapsed in a week two years ago and nobody in your life registered a change, which is not available to anyone drawing from a single employer. nobody registered the recovery either. there is no figure you could write on a form, no clean answer to what is it you do, and every serious conversation about money opens with you dismantling an impression you never built.

lead: you were the big one before you had any say in the matter, and at seventeen you saw a body you have been walking behind ever since, and the distance is where it was.
sun: size is the first fact available about you in a room, and no part of it was ever built. people hand you the heavy end without checking, assume the constitution, assume the appetite is pleasure. you host. you order for the table. nothing in how you eat has ever looked like an account being kept, because a kept account shows on a small person and vanishes completely on you.
moon: the pursuit runs underneath every meal and has done for two decades. a standard set once, by a body that was yours or was somebody else's, never revised since — you measure against it on a wet tuesday with no one in the flat, and it has not moved. the arrangement is never discussed. there is nobody to discuss it with, because from outside, none of this looks like wanting.
pull: no one has ever asked how it is going, because there is no visible version of this. a body that reads as plenty cannot also read as a person twenty years into a chase.
tension: a doctor reads the same numbers on you differently than on a smaller patient, warmly, and sends you home. discipline is the one word nobody has ever put next to your name, because credit for it follows visible change and yours produced none — two decades of a held line looks identical to two decades of not trying. the effort has gone unwitnessed for twenty years, and it holds hardest on the days nobody is there to see it.
cost: you can hold a regime for twenty years on no encouragement, having stopped expecting any around year four, and it has not wobbled once. arrival is what does not come. nobody is placed to tell you that you arrived, having never known you set out, so the only judge available is a standard set at seventeen by a person who had no idea they were setting it.
